cards.explanation: The answer is accept them. The writer opens with "…if you accept my words…" (Proverbs 2:1). Accepting comes before anything else in this whole chain of IFs, friends. You can't unpack a cookie box you never took off the porch.

The answer is False. The verse says "…if you truly call out to insight and lift your voice to understanding…" (Proverbs 2:3). The son uses his voice. He calls out and lifts it. No waiting in silence here, friends.

The answer is silver and hidden treasure, friends. The writer says "…if you seek it like silver and search it out like hidden treasure…" (Proverbs 2:4). Silver and hidden treasure are things people search hard for. That's the kind of seeking the son is told to do.

The answer is the knowledge of God, friends. Verse 5 says "…then you will discern the fear of the LORD and discover the knowledge of God." (Proverbs 2:5). All that searching ends in knowing God. That beats any treasure chest.

The answer is LORD, friends. "For the LORD gives wisdom; from His mouth come knowledge and understanding." (Proverbs 2:6). The son does the searching, and the LORD does the giving. Knowledge and understanding come from His mouth.

The answer is True, friends. Verse 8 says He acts "…to guard the paths of justice and protect the way of His saints." (Proverbs 2:8). So the LORD guards the paths of justice, and He protects the way of His saints. That's a good thing to have on your side.

The answer is False. The verse says "…wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will delight your soul." (Proverbs 2:10). Knowledge doesn't weigh the soul down. It delights it. I'd take that kind of delight any day, friends.

The answer is discretion and understanding, friends. Verse 11 says "Discretion will watch over you, and understanding will guard you…" (Proverbs 2:11). Those two stand watch over him. That's quite a security team.

The answer is True, friends. Verse 14 describes them as "…those who enjoy doing evil and rejoice in the twistedness of evil…" (Proverbs 2:14). They enjoy it and rejoice in it. I think this one is heavy.

The word is crooked, friends. Verse 15 says "…whose paths are crooked and whose ways are devious." (Proverbs 2:15). The paths they walk are crooked, and they're nothing like the straight paths they left.

The answer is the covenant of her God, friends. Verse 17 says she "…abandons the partner of her youth and forgets the covenant of her God." (Proverbs 2:17). Both are things she leaves behind. This is a heavy part, and I think it's a sad picture.

The answer is False, friends. Verse 19 says "None who go to her return or negotiate the paths of life." (Proverbs 2:19). The verse says none who go to her return, and none negotiate the paths of life. It's a heavy warning, and that's why wisdom guards the son from it.

The word is good, friends. Verse 20 says "So you will follow in the ways of the good, and keep to the paths of the righteous." (Proverbs 2:20). With wisdom guarding him, the son follows in the ways of the good. That's the road wisdom leads him down.

The answer is that they inhabit the land and remain in it, friends. Verse 21 says "…the upright will inhabit the land, and the blameless will remain in it…" (Proverbs 2:21). The upright inhabit the land, and the blameless remain in it. I'd say that's a good promise to hear.

The answer is True, friends. Verse 22 says "…but the wicked will be cut off from the land, and the unfaithful will be uprooted." (Proverbs 2:22). The wicked are cut off and the unfaithful are uprooted. It's the sober ending to the two paths.
